facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old Caucasian man
with a history of smoking and cardiovascular disease
presented with a 1-month history of right cheek swelling
He was afebrile
a painless, non-erythematous, mobile, round mass (~2 cm) in the right parotid region
Ultrasonography showed a single lobulated, well-circumscribed, hypoechogenic cystic lesion with irregular edges and acoustic enhancement in the superficial parenchyma of the right parotid gland
a few echogenic foci suggested debris
Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration yielded a cystic background with “dirty” necrosis and pseudopapillary clusters of moderately atypical cells with cyanophilic cytoplasm
The specimen was classified as category V (suspicious for malignancy) by the Milan System
salivary duct carcinoma was initially considered
Contrast-enhanced CT of the face and thorax demonstrated a homogeneously enhancing nodular lesion in the superficial lobe of the right parotid gland
surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule, with no suspicious cervical lymph nodes or thoracic lesions
